topics.label: Lab agent containment failures: OpenAI/Hugging Face and Anthropic eval escapes
topics.notes: Verified at both primary sources this cycle. OpenAI 2026-07-21: models chained priv-esc plus an Artifactory zero-day in the package cache proxy to escape ExploitGym isolation, then breached Hugging Face production. Anthropic 2026-07-30: reviewed 141,006 eval runs, found 3 incidents (6 runs) via Irregular's misconfigured environment; malicious PyPI package live ~1h and executed on 15 real systems; affected orgs had not detected it; Anthropic calls it 'closer to a harness and operational failure than a model alignment failure'. LinkedIn discourse peaking today and mostly sensational or liability-flavored, so the controls-and-observability angle was open. Escalated 2026-08-02.

topics.label: Insuring autonomous agents: Crosby underwrites professional liability for its own agents
topics.notes: New this cycle. Crosby (NewMod law firm) is providing professional liability insurance for its agents so they can do autonomous legal work; Gartner-sourced law.com reporting notes insurers are adding AI exclusions to traditional policies; the Fortune piece on the Anthropic incident closes on the same open question of who is responsible when an autonomous agent causes harm. Firas's lane if it develops: the architecture that makes an agent underwritable (immutable audit trails, deterministic replay, scoped permissions, explainability). Low momentum for now, and the topic must stay engineering-side to avoid anything that reads as legal advice.
